query: Consider the following context: Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications. In that context, which method can be used for tuning the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Tuning the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) can be achieved through compositional engineering.
generation.conditions: Varied composition of elements in the alloy
generation.mechanism: Modification of magnetic exchange interactions and spin ordering
generation.baseline: Untuned magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior of the alloy
generation.boundary: Limits of compositional variability and associated changes in crystal structure
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in predicting the exact compositional dependence of magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior due to the complexity of HEAs

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic variation of alloy composition and measurement of resulting magnetic and magnetocaloric properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no significant correlation between composition and magnetic/magnetocaloric behavior is observed, the hypothesis is falsified
